 J U D G M E N T

Hemavathi vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112748671/
1
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by her in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., the petitioner was traveling on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-08- Q-4133, as a pillion rider, from Mudaram Doddi to their village and while passing near at Bangla Vuru Village, V.Kota Mandalam on V.Kota-Pernumbat NH Road, Chittor District, Andhra Pradesh, a Hyundai Eon Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motor cycle.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter shifted to Government Hospital V.Kota and then referred to PES Hospital, Kuppam,
wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .5,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing housekeeping work at Bengaluru and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
The respondent, being the owner, is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. The respondent not engaged the services of counsel in spite of granting sufficient opportunities and hence, respondent is considered to be contesting the petitioner in her individual capacity.
Respondent not filed the written statement in spite of according opportunities and as such, written statement of respondent is treated nil.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
POINTS 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., near at Bangla vuru village, V.Kota Mandalam, on V.Kota- Pernumbat Road, Chittor District, AP, when petitioner was traveling on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.NO.KA-08-Q- 4133, as a pillion rider, along with family members, due to the rash and negligent driving of Hyundai Eon Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What order or award?

5. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and Medical Record Officer at PES Hospital Kuppam, Chittoor District, A.P., examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14 and closed evidence of her side.
The respondent not adduced evidence on her behalf.

Hemavathi vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112748671/
2
6. Heard the argument of both the side and perused the materials available on record.

The petitioner contended that on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., accident occurred near Bangla vuru village, V.Kota-Pernumbat Road, Chittor District, AP, when petitioner was traveling on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-08-Q-4133, as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver in which she sustained grievous injuries.
9. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.2, first information statement.
On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, one of relatives of petitioner by name Sri.D.M.Venkataramana S/o.
Late Muneppa has lodged complaint with police on 20.05.2024 pertaining to the accident occurred on 19.05.2024.

In the first information statement as well as FIR,
the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.1 discloses the aspect of registration of FIR against the driver of offending car.
The petitioner also furnished spot sketch and its translated copy, which is marked as Ex.P.3 and P.3(a).
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
The respondent not placed any satisfactory materials in order to show that the facts at the place of accident, as described in the sketch, are contrary to the actual facts.
The sketch discloses the aspect of occurrence of accident in the route in which the petitioner has been travelling.
The sketch furnished by petitioner discloses that the offending vehicle came to right side in which the petitioner is going.
The sketch furnished by petitioner also discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.337 & 338 and Sec.146 R/w.196 of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.6.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondent to show that the investigation is not conducted in proper manner.

The, respondent,
being the owner of offending vehicle, does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to Hemavathi vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112748671/
3 have been challenged in any manner.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.

10. The petitioner got examined as PW.1 and filed the affidavit in lieu of chief examination wherein he stated the aspect of occurrence of accident due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondent, though appeared before the Tribunal, not cross examined PW.1 in order to rebut or controvert the contention of petitioner.
The evidence of PW.1 remains unrebutted and unchallenged.

11. No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondent not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondent not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.6, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. Point No.2:
The petitioner succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car vehicle.
As Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., in order to assess the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled.
14. The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained multiple injuries like L1 Wedfe compression fracture and all over the body.

In order to prove the injuries sustained by her,
petitioner has produced wound certificate issued by PES Institute of Medical Sciences & Research Hospital, Bengaluru marked at Ex.P.4.

entities.text: PES Institute of Medical Sciences & Research Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P.4 it reveals that the petitioner sustained L1 wedge compression fracture and the injury is grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.5 - discharge summary issued by PES University Hospital which discloses that she has taken treatment as an inpatient from 19.05.2024 to 22.05.2024 i.e., for a period of 04 days.
The doctor diagnosed that petitioner has sustained L1 wedge compression fracture and underwent medical management and later discharged.
The petitioner has also produced medical bills amounting to .12,075/- marked at Ex.P.7.
The amount mentioned in the advance receipt is included in the discharge bill furnished by petitioner.

Further, the amount mentioned in bill No.3 and 5 has been Hemavathi vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112748671/
4 included in the discharge bill which could be noticed from cumulative split up bill.
The discharge bill discloses that the expenses incurred by petitioner for treatment is .12,075/-.
The amount mentioned in the advance receipt has been deducted from the total bill amount.
As such, the medical expenses is considered to be .12,075/-.
The respondent not furnished satisfactory materials to rebut or disbelieve the medical bills furnished by petitioner.

In order to prove disability,
the petitioner neither produced disability certificate nor examined the doctor.

Further the petitioner got examined the Medical Record Officer at PES Hospital, Kuppam, Chittoor District, A.P. as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.10 to 14 i.e., authorization letter, MLC Register Extract, Police Intimation, case sheet and X-ray films.
The evidence of PW.2 does not disclose the aspect of disability sustained by petitioner.
Evidence of PW.2 is not sufficient and satisfactory in order to assess and ascertain the aspect of disability sustained by petitioner.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove her disability.
The petitioner neither examined any witness nor furnished any materials in order to ascertain the disability stated to have been sustained by her.
The petitioner also not furnished any materials in order to show loss of income as well as loss in her earning capacity due to the accidental injuries.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to consider the impact and effect of accidental injuries to her future.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that the accidental injuries affected the petitioner in carrying out normal activities and caused disability to her.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .75,000/-
(including medical bills).
15.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

entities.text:
Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver.
The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective policy of insurance at the time of accident.
In the absence of valid insurance policy, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
So, the respondent, being the owner of the offending vehicle, is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Point No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Point No.3:-

In view of the findings given on the above said points, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

Hemavathi vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112748671/
5
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
